maya: Heads-up — we're seeing very slow GPU node-pool scale-up in eu-west1 for nightly batch runs. CA waits ages (pods pending >10m) before adding nodes. Any quick tuning tips?

alex: Which cluster-autoscaler flags/expander are you running now? Also cloud provider and node-pool config would help.

maya: Current CA flags (running on GKE):

```
--cloud-provider=gce \
--expander=least-waste \
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m \
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5 \
--max-empty-bulk-delete=10 \
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
```

Node pools: a100-pool (min=0 max=10, taint gpu-type=a100:NoSchedule), v100-pool (min=0 max=5). Pods request `nvidia.com/gpu: 1`, cpu: 8, mem: 64Gi.

lee: least-waste is usually fine, but with mixed GPU types and taints CA can reject expansion if pods don't tolerate target pool taints. Are the pods tolerating `gpu-type=a100`?

maya: Hmm some job templates miss the toleration. That would explain why CA says "no expansion option" even though capacity exists. Example CA log: "scale-up ignored for pod gpu-train-42: insufficient resources in any node group" despite free slots in v100 group.

sam: Two pragmatic changes to try:
1) Use the `priority` expander and assign node-group priorities via label `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/priority: "1000"` on the preferred a100 pool.
2) Ensure pods have correct tolerations and nodeSelector/affinity aligned with pool taints/labels.

alex: Also consider `--max-node-provision-time=15m` if nodes are slow to come up (preemptible or warm start images can delay CA's decision). And enable `--scale-up-from-zero=true` (provider permitting) so CA can scale pools that are at 0.

maya: Good call. I'm seeing CA config that didn't set `max-node-provision-time`. Logs show CA evaluating options and timing out on some attempts.

lee: For GPU workloads, packing is super-sensitive to cpu/mem requests. If requests are oversized (cpu=8), CA may think new node needs to be larger. Try lowering cpu requests to 4 for experiments or use vertical packing with `overhead` if possible.

sam: Also watch scale-down flags — you probably want to avoid aggressive scale-down for GPU pools that cache models. Consider increasing `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to 15m and lowering `--scale-down-utilization-threshold` to 0.3 so CA doesn't remove nodes while jobs are about to start. For preserving nodes used for caching, use `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "false"` annotation on critical pods to prevent eviction/scale-down.

maya: Quick checklist I'm doing tonight:
- add tolerations to all batch job templates
- label a100 pool with priority and switch CA to `--expander=priority`
- set `--max-node-provision-time=15m` on CA
- relax scale-down (15m, util 0.3)
- test reduced cpu requests for a subset of jobs

ops-bot: Scheduled CA deployment restart at 23:00 UTC to roll in new flags. :gear:

alex: When you restart, include `--expander=priority --max-node-provision-time=15m --scale-down-unneeded-time=15m --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.3`. Also keep `--balance-similar-node-groups=true` if you want distributed capacity across similar pools.

sam: One more: annotate node groups with `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/priority` values and keep the cheaper/less-desirable pools with lower priority so CA prefers a100 first (if latency critical). If cost-sensitive, flip priorities.

maya: Update after the change: added tolerations + switched to `priority` expander + set max-provision-time. Early test: a100 pool scaled from 0 -> 1 in ~90s on a small job. Will run full overnight run and report. Thanks all :thumbsup:
